title.zh: 卷一百八十九 列傳第一百十四 高趙田朱
title.en: Volume 189 Biographies 114: Gao, Zhao, Tian, Zhu
title.raw: 卷一百八十九 列傳第一百十四 高趙田朱 Volume 189 Biographies 114: Gao, Zhao, Tian, Zhu

sentences.zh: 高趙田朱

translations.literal: Gao, Zhao, Tian, Zhu
translations.idiomatic: Gao, Zhao, Tian, and Zhu

sentences.zh: 高仁厚，亡其系出。

translations.literal: Gao Renhou; his lineage is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Renhou; his family origins are unknown.

sentences.zh: 初事劍南西川節度使陳敬瑄為營使。

translations.literal: At first he served Chen Jingxuan, military governor of Jiannan West Circuit, as camp commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Chen Jingxuan, military governor of Jiannan West Circuit, as a camp commander.

sentences.zh: 黃巢陷京師，天子出居成都，敬瑄遣黃頭軍部將李鋋鞏鹹以兵萬五千戍興平，數敗巢軍。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao took the capital, the Son of Heaven withdrew to Chengdu; Jingxuan sent the Yellow Head Army generals Li Qian and Gong Xian with fifteen thousand men to garrison Xingping, and they repeatedly defeated Chao's forces.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Chao seized the capital, the emperor withdrew to Chengdu. Chen Jingxuan sent Li Qian and Gong Xian, generals of the Yellow Head Army, with fifteen thousand troops to hold Xingping, and they defeated Chao's army again and again.

sentences.zh: 賊號蜀兵為「鵶兒」，每戰，輒戒曰：「毋與鴉兒鬥。

translations.literal: The rebels called the Shu troops "Crow Boys," and before every battle they would warn, "Do not fight the Crow Boys."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels nicknamed the Shu troops the "Crow Boys," and before each battle they would warn one another, "Do not fight the Crow Boys."

sentences.zh: 」敬瑄喜其兵可用，益選卒二千，使仁厚將而東。

translations.literal: " Jingxuan was pleased that his troops were so effective and selected two thousand more soldiers, sending Renhou east to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan was delighted with their effectiveness, chose another two thousand men, and sent Renhou east at their head.

sentences.zh: 先是，京師有不肖子，皆著疊帶冒，持梃剽閭裏，號「閑子」。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the capital there were worthless young men who all wore layered belts and caps, carried clubs, and plundered the neighborhoods; they were called "idlers."
translations.idiomatic: Before this, worthless youths in the capital wore layered belts and caps, carried clubs, and robbed the neighborhoods; people called them "idlers."

sentences.zh: 京兆尹始視事，輒殺尤者以怖其餘。

translations.literal: When a new Jingzhao intendant took office, he would execute the worst offenders to frighten the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a new Jingzhao intendant took office, he would kill the worst offenders to intimidate the rest.

sentences.zh: 竇潏治京兆，至殺數十百人，稍稍憚戢。

translations.literal: When Dou Yun governed Jingzhao, he killed as many as several hundred people, and the idlers gradually grew fearful and restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dou Yun's administration of Jingzhao, he executed scores of them, until the idlers gradually grew fearful and quieted down.

sentences.zh: 巢入京師，人多避難寶雞，閑子掠之，吏不能制。

translations.literal: When Chao entered the capital, many people fled for refuge to Baoji; the idlers plundered them, and officials could not control it.
translations.idiomatic: After Chao took the capital, many fled to Baoji for safety; the idlers preyed on them, and the authorities could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 仁厚素知狀，下約入邑閭縱擊。

translations.literal: Renhou had long known the situation and issued orders allowing free pursuit within the wards.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou knew the situation well and issued orders permitting unrestricted pursuit within the wards.

sentences.zh: 軍入，閑子聚觀嗤侮，於是殺數千人，坊門反閉，欲亡不得，故皆死，自是閭裏乃安。

translations.literal: When the army entered, the idlers gathered to watch and mock; then several thousand were killed, ward gates were barred from within, and those who wished to flee could not, so all died; from then on the neighborhoods were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops entered, the idlers gathered to jeer; thousands were then killed, ward gates were shut behind them, and none could escape, so all perished. After that the neighborhoods were secure.

sentences.zh: 會邛州賊阡能眾數萬略諸縣，列壁數十，涪州刺史韓秀升等亂峽中，韓求反蜀州，諸將不能定。

translations.literal: At that time the Qianzhou rebel Qian Neng had tens of thousands of followers ravaging the counties and had set up several dozen stockades; Fuzhou prefect Han Xiushang and others were stirring trouble in the gorges, Han Qiu had rebelled in Shuzhou, and the generals could not suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Qianzhou rebel Qian Neng led tens of thousands in raiding the counties and had erected dozens of stockades; Han Xiushang, prefect of Fuzhou, and others were causing turmoil in the gorges, Han Qiu had risen in Shuzhou, and none of the generals could quell them.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄召仁厚還，使督兵四討，屯永安。

translations.literal: Jingxuan recalled Renhou and had him oversee troops on four fronts, encamped at Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan recalled Renhou and put him in command of four columns, encamped at Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 阡能遣諜者入軍中，吏執以獻，諜自言父母妻子囚於賊，約不得軍虛實且死。

translations.literal: Qian Neng sent spies into the army; officials seized and presented them. A spy said his parents, wife, and children were held by the rebels and that he had been bound not to reveal the army's strength or weakness on pain of death.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Neng sent spies into the camp; officers seized and brought them forward. One spy said his parents, wife, and children were hostages of the rebels and that he had been sworn not to disclose the army's condition on pain of death.

sentences.zh: 仁厚哀之，曰：「為我報賊，明日我且戰，有能釋甲迎我者，署背曰『歸順』，皆得復農矣。

translations.literal: Renhou pitied him and said, "Report to the rebels for me: tomorrow I shall give battle. Whoever can lay down arms and welcome me, I shall mark his back with the words 'Returned in Submission' and all may return to farming again."
translations.idiomatic: Renhou took pity on him and said, "Tell the rebels for me: tomorrow I shall fight. Whoever lays down arms to welcome me, I shall mark on his back 'Returned in Submission,' and all may go back to farming."

sentences.zh: 」縱諜去，命諸將毀柵，鼓而前。

translations.literal: " He released the spy and ordered the generals to tear down the palisades and advance to the drum.
translations.idiomatic: He then released the spy, ordered the generals to dismantle the stockades, and advanced to the beat of the drums.

sentences.zh: 賊渠羅渾擎設伏詐降，仁厚遣將不持兵入諭其眾，皆真降。

translations.literal: The rebel chieftain Luo Hunqing set an ambush and feigned surrender; Renhou sent an officer without weapons to persuade the masses, and all truly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Luo Hunqing laid an ambush and feigned surrender; Renhou sent an officer unarmed to address the crowd, and they all submitted in earnest.

sentences.zh: 渾擎詐窮而逸，吏執之，仁厚曰：「愚人不足語。

translations.literal: Hunqing, his ruse exhausted, fled; officers seized him. Renhou said, "A fool is not worth speaking to."
translations.idiomatic: When Hunqing's deception failed he fled; officers seized him. Renhou said, "Fools are not worth reasoning with."

sentences.zh: 」降眾署，皆得免，則告諸壁：「大軍至。

translations.literal: " The surrendered masses were registered and all spared; then they were told at every stockade, "The great army has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: The surrendered men were registered and all spared; then word was sent to every stockade: "The main army has arrived."

sentences.zh: 」賊帥句胡僧大驚，斬之，莫能禁，眾執胡僧以降。

translations.literal: " The rebel leader Gou Huseng was greatly alarmed and beheaded him, but none could stop it; the masses seized Huseng and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief Gou Huseng was terrified and executed him, yet none could restrain the men; they seized Huseng and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 韓求知大賊已禽，徇諸壁曰：「敢出者斬！

translations.literal: Han Qiu, learning that the great rebels had been captured, paraded the stockades saying, "Whoever dares come out will be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Qiu, learning that the major rebels had been taken, proclaimed through the stockades, "Whoever dares come out will be executed!"

sentences.zh: 」眾罵之，求赴水死，眾鉤出，斬以徇，余柵皆下。

translations.literal: " The masses cursed him; Qiu sought death by drowning, but the crowd hooked him out, beheaded him as a warning, and the remaining stockades all came down.
translations.idiomatic: The men cursed him; Qiu tried to drown himself, but they hauled him out with hooks, beheaded him as a warning, and the rest of the stockades submitted.

sentences.zh: 仁厚按轡徘徊視賊壘，吏請焚之，仁厚命取財糧，乃縱火，屍賊成都。

translations.literal: Renhou held the reins and paced about viewing the rebel fortifications; officials asked to burn them, but Renhou ordered the wealth and grain taken first, then set fire; the rebel corpses filled Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou rode slowly about the rebel camps; officers asked to burn them, but he ordered the goods and grain removed first, then set them ablaze. Rebel corpses filled Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 仁厚還，天子禦樓勞軍，授仁厚檢校尚書左仆射、眉州刺史。

translations.literal: Renhou returned; the Son of Heaven appeared on the tower to reward the army and appointed Renhou acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and prefect of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Renhou returned, the emperor appeared on the tower to honor the troops and appointed him acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and prefect of Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄與仁厚謀曰：「秀升未禽，貢輸梗奪，百官乏奉，民不鹽食。

translations.literal: Jingxuan said to Renhou in counsel, "Xiushang is not yet captured; tribute and transport are cut off, the hundred officials lack stipends, and the people have no salt to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan told Renhou in counsel, "Xiushang is not yet taken; tribute and transport are blocked, the court officials have no stipends, and the people lack salt."

sentences.zh: 公能破賊，當以東川待公。

translations.literal: If you can break the rebels, Dongchuan shall be yours.
translations.idiomatic: If you can defeat the rebels, Dongchuan will be yours."

sentences.zh: 」仁厚許之。

translations.literal: " Renhou agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔拜行軍司馬。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him acting army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him acting army marshal.

sentences.zh: 仁厚聞賊儲械、子女皆在屯，乃以銳兵瀕江，伐木頹水礙舟道，負岸而陣。

translations.literal: Renhou heard that the rebels' stored arms and women and children were all in the camp; he therefore took crack troops along the river, felled trees to block the current and obstruct the channel, and formed battle lines with their backs to the bank.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the rebels' arms, dependents, and stores were all in the camp, he posted elite troops along the river, felled trees into the current to block the channel, and drew up his lines with their backs to the shore.

sentences.zh: 使遊軍逼賊，久不戰，則夜以千卒持短刀、強弩直薄營，火而噪之。

translations.literal: He sent skirmishers to press the rebels; when there was no battle for a long time, at night he sent a thousand men with short swords and powerful crossbows straight into the camp, setting fires and raising a clamor.
translations.idiomatic: He sent light troops to harry the rebels; when fighting stalled, at night he sent a thousand men with short swords and strong crossbows straight into the camp, setting fires and raising an uproar.

sentences.zh: 秀升率舟兵救火，仁厚遣人鶩沒鑿舟，皆沈，眾懼，多潰。

translations.literal: Xiushang led boat troops to fight the fire; Renhou sent men diving like ducks to bore holes in the boats, and all sank; the masses were afraid and many fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushang led his river force to fight the blaze; Renhou sent men diving to bore through the boats, and all sank. The rebels panicked and many fled.

sentences.zh: 秀升斬潰兵，欲脅止之，眾怒，執秀升以降。

translations.literal: Xiushang beheaded the fleeing soldiers, hoping to intimidate them into stopping, but the masses were enraged and seized Xiushang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushang executed the fugitives to force them back, but the men were furious and seized him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 仁厚問狀，對曰：「天子蒙塵，反者何獨我？

translations.literal: Renhou questioned him; he replied, "The Son of Heaven is in distress; why am I alone a rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: Renhou questioned him; he answered, "The emperor is in distress—why should I alone be called a rebel?"

sentences.zh: 」仁厚檻車送行在，斬於市。

translations.literal: " Renhou sent him in a caged cart to the imperial presence and executed him in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou sent him in a prisoner cart to the emperor's camp and had him beheaded in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 東川節度使楊師立初隸神策軍，累遷檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Yang Shili, military governor of Dongchuan, had first served in the Shence Army and was repeatedly promoted to acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Councilor of the State Chancellery with the Tong rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shili, military governor of Dongchuan, had first served in the Imperial Shence Army and rose to acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Councilor with the Tong rank.

sentences.zh: 聞敬瑄仁厚代己，有望言。

translations.literal: Hearing that Jingxuan and Renhou would replace him, he spoke words of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Chen Jingxuan and Renhou were to replace him, he spoke bitterly of it.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄諷帝召師立以本官兼尚書右仆射，師立益怒，移檄言敬瑄十罪，殺監軍田繪，屯涪城，遣兵攻綿州，不克。

translations.literal: Jingxuan prompted the emperor to summon Shili with his existing office and also as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Shili grew angrier, circulated a proclamation listing ten crimes of Jingxuan, killed the supervising commissioner Tian Hui, encamped at Fucheng, and sent troops to attack Mianzhou without success.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan urged the emperor to recall Shili with his existing rank and also as Right Vice Director; Shili grew still angrier, issued a manifesto listing ten crimes against Jingxuan, killed the supervising commissioner Tian Hui, encamped at Fucheng, and sent troops against Mianzhou without success.

sentences.zh: 又檄劍州刺史姚卓文共攻成都，假卓文為指揮應接使，卓文不應。

translations.literal: He also summoned Jianzhou prefect Yao Zhuowen to join in attacking Chengdu, appointing Zhuowen acting commander for liaison, but Zhuowen did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: He also called on Jianzhou prefect Yao Zhuowen to attack Chengdu jointly, naming Zhuowen acting liaison commander, but Zhuowen refused.

sentences.zh: 帝乃下詔削官爵。

translations.literal: The emperor then issued an edict stripping his titles.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then stripped him of rank and titles by edict.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄即表仁厚為東川節度留後，楊茂言為行軍副使，楊棠為諸軍都虞候，率兵三萬討之。

translations.literal: Jingxuan immediately memorialized Renhou as acting military governor of Dongchuan, Yang Maoyan as acting army vice marshal, and Yang Tang as chief commander of all armies, and led thirty thousand troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan at once recommended Renhou as acting governor of Dongchuan, Yang Maoyan as acting army vice marshal, and Yang Tang as chief commander of all armies, and marched thirty thousand men against him.

sentences.zh: 師立遣大將張士安、鄭君雄守鹿頭關。

translations.literal: Shili sent his great generals Zhang Shi'an and Zheng Junxiong to hold Lutou Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Shili sent his chief generals Zhang Shi'an and Zheng Junxiong to defend Lutou Pass.

sentences.zh: 仁厚次漢州，前軍戰德陽，師立嬰城，閱四旬，夜出兵擾北柵，仁厚設兩翼而伏，披柵門列炬，賊不敢進，伏發，擊走之。

translations.literal: Renhou halted at Hanzhou; the vanguard fought at Deyang; Shili clung to the city. After forty days, at night he sent troops to harass the northern stockade; Renhou set wings in ambush, threw open the stockade gates and lined torches, the rebels dared not enter, the ambush struck, and they were driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou encamped at Hanzhou while the vanguard fought at Deyang; Shili held the city. After forty days he raided the northern camp by night; Renhou posted wings in ambush, flung open the stockade gates with torches blazing, the rebels dared not enter, the ambush rose, and they were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 楊茂言謂仁厚且敗，引兵走，久乃還。

translations.literal: Yang Maoyan thought Renhou was about to be defeated and led his troops away, returning only after a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Maoyan thought Renhou was on the verge of defeat and withdrew; only after a long interval did he return.

sentences.zh: 明日，會諸將，仁厚曰：「副使當以死報天子。

translations.literal: The next day he assembled the generals; Renhou said, "The vice marshal ought to die to repay the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he convened the generals. Renhou said, "The vice marshal should die to repay the emperor."

sentences.zh: 」斬而徇。

translations.literal: " He beheaded him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded him as a warning.

sentences.zh: 於是士安不敢出，師立自督士，十戰皆北。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shi'an dared not come out; Shili personally led the troops, and in ten battles all were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an then dared not emerge; Shili personally led the men, and in ten engagements all were beaten.

sentences.zh: 仁厚約城中斬首惡者賞，君雄呼於軍曰：「天子所討，反者耳，吾等何與？

translations.literal: Renhou promised reward to whoever in the city beheaded the chief villain; Junxiong called out to the army, "The Son of Heaven is punishing rebels only—what have we to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: Renhou promised rewards to anyone in the city who slew the ringleader; Junxiong shouted to the troops, "The emperor is punishing rebels only—what is that to us?"

sentences.zh: 」乃與士安嘩而進，以仁厚書示師立曰：「請以死謝眾。

translations.literal: " Then he and Shi'an clamored and advanced, showing Shili Renhou's letter and saying, "Please die to answer the masses."
translations.idiomatic: He and Shi'an then stormed forward with an uproar, showed Shili Renhou's letter, and said, "Please die to satisfy the men."

sentences.zh: 」自沈於池死。

translations.literal: " He drowned himself in a pool and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shili drowned himself in a pool.

sentences.zh: 君雄悉誅其家，獻首天子。

translations.literal: Junxiong executed his entire family and presented his head to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Junxiong put his whole household to death and sent his head to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 仁厚入府，縱系囚，賑貧絕。

translations.literal: Renhou entered the headquarters, released the imprisoned, and relieved the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou entered the prefectural seat, freed the prisoners, and aided the destitute.

sentences.zh: 詔拜劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，遂據梓州，絕敬瑄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi he then seized Zizhou and cut off Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangqi he seized Zizhou and broke with Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 君雄時為遂州刺史，亦陷漢州，攻成都。

translations.literal: Junxiong was then prefect of Suizhou; he also took Hanzhou and attacked Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Junxiong was then prefect of Suizhou; he also captured Hanzhou and attacked Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄使部將李順之逆戰，君雄死。

translations.literal: Jingxuan sent his officer Li Shunzhi to meet him in battle, and Junxiong died.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan sent his officer Li Shunzhi to oppose him, and Junxiong was killed.

sentences.zh: 又發維、茂州羌軍擊仁厚，斬之。

translations.literal: He also raised Qiang troops from Wei and Mao prefectures to strike Renhou and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He also mobilized Qiang forces from Wei and Mao prefectures against Renhou and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，皆追贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the Qianning era all were posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Masters.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianning they were all posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Masters.

sentences.zh: 趙犨，陳州宛丘人，世為忠武軍牙將。

translations.literal: Zhao Chou, a native of Wanshou in Chenzhou, for generations a junior general of the Loyal and Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chou was from Wanshou in Chenzhou; his family for generations had served as junior generals of the Loyal and Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 犨資警健，兒弄時好為營陣行列，自號令指顧，群兒無敢亂。

translations.literal: Chou was by nature alert and robust; as a child at play he liked to form camp arrays and ranks, giving orders and gestures himself, and none of the boys dared misbehave.
translations.idiomatic: Chou was sharp and sturdy by nature; as a boy at play he liked to form camp lines and ranks, issuing orders himself, and none of the other children dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 父叔文見之，曰：「是當大吾門。

translations.literal: His father Shuwen saw this and said, "This one will enlarge our house."
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuwen saw it and said, "This boy will bring greatness to our house."

sentences.zh: 」稍長，喜書，學擊劍，善射。

translations.literal: " As he grew he loved books, studied swordplay, and was skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he took to books, studied swordsmanship, and became an able archer.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，從伐潞州，收天井關，又從征蠻，忠武軍功多，遷大校。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era he followed the campaign against Luzhou, took Tianjing Pass, and again followed the expedition against the barbarians; the Loyal and Martial Army won many merits, and he was promoted to senior commander.
translations.idiomatic: During Huichang he joined the campaign against Luzhou and took Tianjing Pass, then joined the southern expedition; the Loyal and Martial Army won great credit, and he was promoted to senior commander.

sentences.zh: 黃巢入長安，所在盜興，陳人詣節度府，請犨為刺史，表於朝，授之。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao entered Chang'an, bandits rose everywhere; the people of Chen went to the circuit headquarters and asked that Chou be made prefect; they memorialized the court and he was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao entered Chang'an, brigands rose everywhere; the people of Chen went to the circuit seat and asked that Chou be made prefect; a memorial was sent to court and he was appointed.

sentences.zh: 既視事，會官屬計曰：「巢若不死長安，必東出關，陳其沖也。

translations.literal: Once he took office he met with his staff and said, "If Chao does not die in Chang'an, he will surely march east through the passes; Chen is the choke point."
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he met his staff and said, "If Chao is not destroyed in Chang'an, he will surely march east through the passes—and Chen lies in his path."

sentences.zh: 」乃培城疏塹，實倉庫，峙槁薪，為守計。

translations.literal: " They therefore raised the walls, cleared the moats, filled the granaries, piled fuel, and made plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: They raised the walls, deepened the moats, filled the granaries, stockpiled fuel, and prepared to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 民有貲者悉內之，繕甲兵，募悍勇，悉補子弟領兵。

translations.literal: Wealthy citizens were all required to bring in their goods; armor and weapons were repaired; fierce men were recruited; and all were assigned as officers under his sons and younger kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy were required to deposit their goods within; arms were repaired; bold men were recruited; and all were placed under his sons and kinsmen as officers.

sentences.zh: 巢敗，果東奔。

translations.literal: When Chao was defeated, he indeed fled east.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao was defeated, he did indeed flee east.

sentences.zh: 賊將孟楷以萬人寇項，犨擊禽之。

translations.literal: The rebel general Meng Kai led ten thousand men to raid Xiang; Chou attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Meng Kai led ten thousand men against Xiang; Chou attacked and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 僖宗嘉其功，遷累檢校司空。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong praised his achievement and repeatedly promoted him to acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong praised his achievement and repeatedly promoted him to acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 巢聞楷死，驚且怒，悉軍據溵水，與秦宗權合兵數十萬，繚長壕五周，百道攻之。

translations.literal: Chao, hearing that Kai had died, was both shocked and enraged; he gathered his whole army at Yinshui, joined Qin Zongquan with several hundred thousand men, ringed the city with five lines of long trenches, and attacked on a hundred fronts.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao heard that Kai had been killed, he was shocked and furious; he massed his entire force at Yinshui, joined Qin Zongquan with hundreds of thousands of men, dug five rings of long trenches around the city, and assaulted it on every side.

sentences.zh: 州人大恐，犨令曰：「士貴建功立名節，今雖眾寡不敵，男子當死地求生，徒懼無益也。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture were greatly afraid; Chou ordered, "A gentleman values establishing merit and preserving honor; though we are few against many, a man should seek life in a place of death—mere fear is of no use.
translations.idiomatic: The people were terrified; Chou proclaimed, "Men prize merit and honor; though we are outnumbered, let each seek life where death threatens—fear alone avails nothing.

sentences.zh: 且死國，不愈生為賊乎？

translations.literal: To die for the state—is that not better than living as a rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: Is it not better to die for the state than to live as a rebel's slave?"

sentences.zh: 吾家食陳祿，誓破賊以保陳，異議者斬！

translations.literal: Our house has eaten Chen's stipends; I swear to break the rebels and preserve Chen—whoever disagrees, beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: My family has lived on Chen's pay; I swear to break the rebels and save Chen—whoever objects, beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 」眾聽命。

translations.literal: " The masses obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The men obeyed.

sentences.zh: 引銳士出戰，屢破賊。

translations.literal: He led crack troops out to battle and repeatedly defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He led elite troops out repeatedly and broke the rebel forces again and again.

sentences.zh: 巢益怒，將必屠之，乃起八仙營於州左，僭象宮闕，列百官曹署，儲糧為持久計。

translations.literal: Chao grew still angrier and resolved to slaughter the city utterly; he therefore raised the Eight Immortals Camp east of the prefecture, usurping the likeness of palace halls, arraying the hundred officials' offices, and storing grain for a prolonged siege.
translations.idiomatic: Chao grew still more furious and vowed to slaughter the city; he built the Eight Immortals Camp east of the seat, mimicking palace halls, setting up offices for the hundred officials, and hoarding grain for a long siege.

sentences.zh: 宗權輸鎧仗軍須，賊益張。

translations.literal: Zongquan supplied armor, weapons, and army provisions, and the rebels grew still bolder.
translations.idiomatic: Zongquan sent armor, weapons, and supplies, and the rebels grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 犨小大數百戰，勝負相當，故人心固，乃間道乞師於朱全忠。

translations.literal: Chou fought great and small engagements several hundred times, victories and defeats roughly equal, so the people's hearts held firm; he then sent envoys by secret route to beg troops from Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chou fought several hundred engagements large and small, with fortunes roughly even, so morale held; he then sent envoys by a hidden route to beg aid from Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，汴軍至，壁西北，陳人思奮，犨引兵急擊賊，破之。

translations.literal: Before long the Bian army arrived and encamped northwest; the people of Chen were eager to fight; Chou led troops in a swift assault and broke the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Bian troops arrived and camped to the northwest; the people of Chen were eager to strike; Chou led a fierce assault and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 圍凡三百日而解。

translations.literal: The siege, in all three hundred days, was then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege, which had lasted three hundred days, was lifted.

sentences.zh: 中和五年，擢彰義軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhonghe he was promoted to military governor of Zhangyi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhonghe he was made military governor of Zhangyi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 巢雖敗，宗權始熾，略地數千里，屠二十餘州，唯陳賴犨獨完，以功檢校司徒，加泰寧、浙西兩節度，皆在陳並領之。

translations.literal: Though Chao had been defeated, Zongquan now flourished, seizing territory for thousands of li and slaughtering more than twenty prefectures; only Chen, relying on Chou, remained intact; for his merit he was made acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and given the two circuits of Taining and Zhexi, all administered from Chen concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chao had fallen, Zongquan now rose powerful, seizing lands for thousands of li and slaughtering more than twenty prefectures; only Chen, through Chou, stood intact; for this he was made acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and given Taining and Zhexi as well, all governed from Chen at once.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，進同中書門下平章事、忠武軍節度，仍治陳州，流亡踵還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji he was advanced to Grand Councilor with the Tong rank and military governor of the Loyal and Martial Army, still governing Chenzhou; refugees returned in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Longji he was made Grand Councilor with the Tong rank and governor of the Loyal and Martial Army, still at Chenzhou, and exiles streamed back.

sentences.zh: 與弟昶至友愛，後將老，悉以軍事付之，乃卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Chang were deeply affectionate; when he grew old he entrusted all military affairs to him, then died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He and his brother Chang were devoted to each other; as he aged he handed all military affairs to him, then died and was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 犨悉忠力以孤城抗賊，巢卒敗亡。

translations.literal: Chou devoted his full loyalty and strength to holding a lone city against the rebels, and Chao was ultimately defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chou gave his full loyalty and strength to hold a lone city against the rebels, and Chao was ultimately broken and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 然附全忠，亦賴其力復振，故委輸調發助全忠，常先它鎮雲。

translations.literal: Yet he attached himself to Quanzhong and also relied on his strength to recover; therefore he sent tribute and supplies to aid Quanzhong, often ahead of the other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he aligned with Quanzhong and relied on his power to recover; he therefore sent tribute and supplies to aid him, often ahead of every other circuit.

sentences.zh: 昶，字大東，神采軒異，而內沈厚，有法度。

translations.literal: Chang, styled Dadong, had a striking presence and carriage, yet inwardly was deep and steady, with a sense of measure.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, courtesy name Dadong, had a striking bearing, yet inwardly was deep and steady and governed by rule.

sentences.zh: 破孟楷功多。

translations.literal: In defeating Meng Kai his merit was great.
translations.idiomatic: His merit in defeating Meng Kai was great.

sentences.zh: 巢之圍，昶夜掫師，疲而寢，如有神相之者。

translations.literal: During Chao's siege, Chang led the night patrol; weary, he slept, yet it was as if a spirit watched over him.
translations.idiomatic: During Chao's siege Chang led the night watch; exhausted, he would sleep, yet it seemed a spirit stood guard over him.

sentences.zh: 犁曙決戰，士爭奮死鬥，禽賊酋數人，斬級千餘。

translations.literal: At dawn he joined the decisive battle; the soldiers strove to fight to the death; several rebel chiefs were captured and more than a thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he joined the decisive fight; the men fought desperately; several rebel chiefs were taken and more than a thousand heads were cut off.

sentences.zh: 犨領泰寧，以昶為州刺史、檢校尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: Chou held Taining and made Chang prefect of the prefecture and acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Chou held Taining he made Chang prefect there and acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 當時，方鎮言忠壯吏治，舉言犨、昶。

translations.literal: At the time, among the circuits when one spoke of loyal fortitude and able governance, all named Chou and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, whenever the circuits spoke of loyal courage and sound administration, they named Chou and Chang.

sentences.zh: 犨之老，乃授留後，遷忠武節度使，亦留陳。

translations.literal: When Chou grew old he handed over the acting governorship; he was transferred to military governor of the Loyal and Martial Army but still remained at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: As Chou aged he transferred the acting governorship; he was promoted to governor of the Loyal and Martial Army but still stayed at Chen.

sentences.zh: 進檢校司徒。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 劭勸農桑，於人有恩惠。

translations.literal: Shao encouraged agriculture and sericulture and showed kindness to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Shao encouraged farming and sericulture and treated the people with kindness.

sentences.zh: 加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was added as Grand Councilor with the Tong rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Councilor with the Tong rank.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年卒，年五十三，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianning he died at fifty-three and was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianning he died at fifty-three and was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 犨子珝，字有節。

translations.literal: Chou's son Xu, styled Youjie.
translations.idiomatic: Chou's son Xu, courtesy name Youjie.

sentences.zh: 雄毅喜書，善騎射。

translations.literal: Bold and resolute, he loved books and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and resolute, loved books, and was skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 巢之難，激勵麾下，約皆死。

translations.literal: During Chao's calamity he roused his subordinates and bound them all to die.
translations.idiomatic: During Huang Chao's rebellion he roused his men and bound them all to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 以先冢邇賊，畏見殘齮，即夜縋死士取柩以入。

translations.literal: Because his ancestors' tombs lay near the rebels, fearing they would be desecrated, he sent elite men down ropes by night to bring the coffins within the walls.
translations.idiomatic: His family tombs lay close to the rebels; fearing desecration, he sent daredevils down ropes by night to haul the coffins inside the city.

sentences.zh: 庫有巨弩，機牙壞，不能張，珝以意調治，激矢至五百步，人馬皆洞，賊畏不敢逼。

translations.literal: In the arsenal was a great crossbow whose mechanism was broken and could not be drawn; Xu repaired it by intuition, and when the bolt was released it flew five hundred paces, piercing men and horses through; the rebels feared it and dared not press close.
translations.idiomatic: The arsenal held a great crossbow with broken gears that would not draw; Xu restored it by instinct, and its bolts flew five hundred paces, piercing men and horses; the rebels feared it and dared not close in.

sentences.zh: 以勞檢校尚書右仆射，遙領處州刺史。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and held the prefecture of Chuzhou in title only.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made acting Right Vice Director and given nominal governorship of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 昶帥忠武，珝遷行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Chang commanded the Loyal and Martial Army, Xu was transferred to acting army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang led the Loyal and Martial Army, Xu was promoted to acting army marshal.

sentences.zh: 昶之喪，知忠武留後，政簡濟，上下安之。

translations.literal: At Chang's funeral he became acting governor of the Loyal and Martial Army; his government was simple and effective, and superiors and subordinates were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: On Chang's death he became acting governor; his rule was simple and effective, and all were content.

sentences.zh: 全忠表為忠武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Quanzhong memorialized him as military governor of the Loyal and Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong recommended him as military governor of the Loyal and Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 陳土惡善圮，珝疊甓表墉，遂無患。

translations.literal: The soil of Chen was poor and walls easily crumbled; Xu faced the outer wall with layered bricks, and thereafter there was no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's soil was weak and walls crumbled easily; Xu faced the outer wall with layered brick, and the problem ceased.

sentences.zh: 三加檢校太保。

translations.literal: Three times he was advanced to acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was three times advanced to acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 光化三年，同中書門下平章事，進兼侍中，封天水郡公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guanghua he was made Grand Councilor with the Tong rank, advanced to concurrent Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed Duke of Tianshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guanghua he became Grand Councilor with the Tong rank, was made concurrent Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed Duke of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 按鄧艾故跡，決翟王渠溉稻以利農。

translations.literal: Following Deng Ai's old traces, he opened the Zhaiwang Canal to irrigate rice fields for the benefit of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Following Deng Ai's old works, he opened the Zhaiwang Canal to irrigate the fields and aid the farmers.

sentences.zh: 一家三節度，相繼二十餘年，陳人宜之。

translations.literal: One family held three governorships in succession for more than twenty years, and the people of Chen were content with it.
translations.idiomatic: One family held three circuit governorships in succession for more than twenty years, and the people of Chen were well pleased.

sentences.zh: 天復初，韓建帥忠武，以珝知同州節度留後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, Han Jian commanded the Loyal and Martial Army and made Xu acting governor of Tongzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianfu, Han Jian led the Loyal and Martial Army and made Xu acting governor of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 昭宗還長安，詔入朝，賜號「迎鑾功臣」。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, an edict summoned him to court and bestowed the title "Meritorious Minister Who Welcomed the Imperial Carriage."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, he was summoned to court and granted the title "Meritorious Minister Who Welcomed the Imperial Carriage."

sentences.zh: 以檢校太傅為右金吾衛上將軍，從東遷。

translations.literal: As acting Grand Mentor he was made General-in-Chief of the Right Golden Crow Guard and followed the eastward migration.
translations.idiomatic: As acting Grand Mentor he became General-in-Chief of the Right Golden Crow Guard and followed the court east.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以疾免。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was relieved for illness.
translations.idiomatic: After a year and more he was dismissed on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十五，贈侍中，陳人為罷市。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-five; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, and the people of Chen closed the markets in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-five and was posthumously made Palace Attendant; the people of Chen closed the markets in mourning.

sentences.zh: 田頵，字德臣，廬州合肥人。

translations.literal: Tian Yun, styled Dechen, was a native of Hefei in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yun, courtesy name Dechen, was from Hefei in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 略通書傳，沈果有大誌。

translations.literal: He had some knowledge of books and classics; deep and resolute, he harbored great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: He had some learning in the classics; he was deep and resolute and nursed great ambitions.

sentences.zh: 與楊行密同裏，約為兄弟。

translations.literal: He was from the same neighborhood as Yang Xingmi and they pledged brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in the same neighborhood as Yang Xingmi and they swore brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 應州募屯邊，遷主將。

translations.literal: He answered the prefecture's call to garrison the frontier and was promoted to chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: He answered the prefecture's frontier levy and rose to chief commander.

sentences.zh: 行密據廬州，頵謀為多。

translations.literal: When Xingmi held Luzhou, Yun's stratagems were many.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingmi seized Luzhou, Yun's stratagems were numerous.

sentences.zh: 攻趙锽於宣州，锽出東溪，乘暴流以逸，阻水解甲，謂追騎不能及。

translations.literal: Attacking Zhao Chuan at Xuanzhou, Chuan fled by the eastern stream, riding the raging current to escape; blocked by the water he doffed his armor, thinking the pursuing horsemen could not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Zhao Chuan at Xuanzhou, Chuan fled down the eastern stream on the flood, doffed his armor at the ford, and thought the pursuers could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 頵乘輕舠追之，锽驚，遂見禽。

translations.literal: Yun pursued in a light boat; Chuan was alarmed and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yun chased him in a light skiff; Chuan was startled and was taken.

sentences.zh: 行密表頵為馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: Xingmi memorialized Yun as chief commander of horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi recommended Yun as chief commander of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 沙陀叛將安仁義奔淮南，行密大喜，屬以騎兵，使在頵右，兩人名冠軍中，共攻常州，殺刺史杜棱。

translations.literal: The Shatuo rebel An Renyi fled to Huainan; Xingmi was greatly pleased, entrusted him with cavalry, and placed him on Yun's right; the two men's names topped the army; together they attacked Changzhou and killed prefect Du Ling.
translations.idiomatic: The Shatuo rebel An Renyi fled to Huainan; Xingmi was delighted, gave him the cavalry, and posted him beside Yun; the two were the army's finest; together they took Changzhou and killed prefect Du Ling.

sentences.zh: 錢镠方屯潤州，一夕潰。

translations.literal: Qian Liu was then encamped at Runzhou and fled in a single night.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu was encamped at Runzhou and broke in one night.

sentences.zh: 會孫儒南略，頵等屯丹陽，儒火揚州，壁廣德，頵破其屯。

translations.literal: When Sun Ru marched south, Yun and others encamped at Danyang; Ru burned Yangzhou and walled Guangde; Yun broke his camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ru advanced south, Yun and others held Danyang; Ru burned Yangzhou and fortified Guangde; Yun routed his camp.

sentences.zh: 與戰，頵走，行密怒，奪其兵。

translations.literal: In battle Yun fled; Xingmi was angry and stripped him of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In battle Yun fled; Xingmi was furious and took away his command.

sentences.zh: 或諫行密曰：「強敵傅壘，不用頵，非計也。

translations.literal: Someone advised Xingmi, "A strong enemy is pressing the ramparts; not to use Yun is no plan."
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Xingmi, "A strong foe is on the walls; to leave Yun unused is poor strategy."

sentences.zh: 」行密復將頵。

translations.literal: " Xingmi again put Yun in command.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi again gave Yun command.

sentences.zh: 儒詒書仁義通好，以疑行密，行密待益厚，署行軍副使，卒用此二人功禽儒。

translations.literal: Ru sent a deceitful letter to Renyi proposing friendship to sow doubt in Xingmi; Xingmi treated him still more generously, appointed him acting army vice marshal, and in the end by these two men's merit captured Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Ru wrote Renyi feigning friendship to unsettle Xingmi; Xingmi treated him more generously still, made him acting army vice marshal, and finally through the two men captured Ru.

sentences.zh: 乃表仁義為潤州刺史，頵寧國軍節度使。

translations.literal: He then memorialized Renyi as prefect of Runzhou and Yun as military governor of Ningguo Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Renyi as prefect of Runzhou and Yun as governor of Ningguo Circuit.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校太保、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to acting Grand Guardian and Grand Councilor with the Tong rank.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to acting Grand Guardian and Grand Councilor with the Tong rank.

sentences.zh: 仁義至檢校太保。

translations.literal: Renyi reached acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi rose to acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 頵已平馮弘鐸，至揚州謝行密。

translations.literal: Yun had already pacified Feng Hongduo and came to Yangzhou to thank Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Feng Hongduo, Yun came to Yangzhou to thank Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 左右求貲不已，獄吏亦有請，頵怒曰：「吏覬吾入獄邪！

translations.literal: His attendants endlessly sought bribes, and prison officers also made requests; Yun grew angry and said, "Do the officers expect me to enter prison?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants endlessly demanded gifts, and jailers too asked for favors; Yun raged, "Do you officers expect me in prison?"

sentences.zh: 」又求池、歙為屬州，行密不許，頵始怨。

translations.literal: " He also asked that Chi and She be made subordinate prefectures; Xingmi refused, and Yun began to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: He also demanded Chi and She as subordinate prefectures; Xingmi refused, and Yun began to bear a grudge.

sentences.zh: 將還，指府門曰：「吾不復入此。」

translations.literal: As he was about to return, he pointed at the headquarters gate and said, "I shall not enter here again."
translations.idiomatic: About to leave, he pointed at the gate and said, "I will never enter this place again."

sentences.zh: 是時，錢镠部將徐綰叛，镠入杭州逐綰，綰屯靈隱山迎頵。

translations.literal: At that time Qian Liu's officer Xu Wan rebelled; Liu entered Hangzhou to drive Wan out; Wan encamped on Lingyin Mountain to welcome Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qian Liu's officer Xu Wan rebelled; Liu entered Hangzhou to expel him; Wan camped on Lingyin Mountain to welcome Yun.

sentences.zh: 頵遣客何曉見镠曰：「王宜東保會稽，無為虛屠士眾也。

translations.literal: Yun sent his guest He Xiao to see Liu and say, "Your Highness should hold Kuaiji in the east and not slaughter your soldiers in vain."
translations.idiomatic: Yun sent He Xiao to Liu: "Your Highness should secure Kuaiji in the east and not waste your men in vain."

sentences.zh: 」镠曰：「軍中小叛常然，公為人長，何助逆耶？

translations.literal: " Liu said, "Small rebellions in an army are common; you are an elder—why aid treason?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu replied, "Petty mutinies are common in armies; you are an elder—why help rebels?"

sentences.zh: 」頵攻北門，镠登城與語，射中麾下。

translations.literal: " Yun attacked the north gate; Liu mounted the wall to speak with him and shot one of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Yun assaulted the north gate; Liu mounted the wall to parley and struck down one of his men.

sentences.zh: 頵築壘絕往來道，镠患之，出金幣十輿，募能奪地者。

translations.literal: Yun built stockades to cut the roads; Liu was troubled and offered ten cartloads of gold and coins to recruit men who could seize the ground back.
translations.idiomatic: Yun walled off the roads; Liu, distressed, offered ten cartloads of gold to whoever could retake the ground.

sentences.zh: 陳璋以死士三百，免胄馳擊，奪其地，镠授璋衢州刺史。

translations.literal: Chen Zhang led three hundred death-fighters, bareheaded and charging at full gallop, seized the position, and Liu appointed Zhang prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhang led three hundred daredevils bareheaded at full charge, retook the ground, and Liu made him prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 頵攻城未能克，將濟江絕西陵，為镠將所卻，圍益急。

translations.literal: Yun could not take the city; about to cross the river to cut Xiling, he was driven back by Liu's generals and the siege grew tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Yun failed to storm the city; as he prepared to cross the river and sever Xiling, Liu's generals repulsed him and the encirclement tightened.

sentences.zh: 先是，行密欲女镠子，镠急，乃遣元迎女，且告行密曰：「頵得誌，為患必大，請以子為質，願召還頵。

translations.literal: Earlier Xingmi had wished to marry his daughter to Liu's son; Liu was urgent and sent Yuan to welcome the bride, and also told Xingmi, "If Yun succeeds, the harm will be great; please take my son as hostage and recall Yun."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xingmi had sought Liu's son for his daughter; Liu in haste sent Yuan to fetch the bride and told Xingmi, "If Yun prevails the harm will be great—take my son hostage and recall Yun."

sentences.zh: 」行密使人謂頵曰：「不還，我遣人代守宣州。

translations.literal: " Xingmi sent someone to tell Yun, "If you do not return, I shall send another to hold Xuanzhou in your stead."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent word: "If you do not return, I will send another to guard Xuanzhou."

sentences.zh: 」頵不從。

translations.literal: " Yun would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Yun refused.

sentences.zh: 镠輸錢二百萬緡犒軍，頵又請镠子元瓘出質，乃與綰引兵還。

translations.literal: Liu paid two million strings in cash to reward the army; Yun also demanded Liu's son Yuan Guan as hostage; then he and Wan led their troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Liu paid two million strings to reward the troops; Yun also demanded Yuan Guan as hostage; then he and Wan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 然內怨行密與镠，因移書曰：「侯王守方以奉天子，譬百川不朝於海，雖狂奔澶漫，終為涸土，不若順流無窮也。

translations.literal: Yet inwardly he resented Xingmi and Liu and therefore sent a letter saying, "Princes and marquises guard their territories to serve the Son of Heaven; it is like the hundred streams not paying court to the sea—though they rush wildly and flood, in the end they become dry earth; better to follow the current without end."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he resented Xingmi and Liu and wrote, "Lords guard their lands for the emperor, as streams must reach the sea—though they rage and flood, they end as dry soil; better to flow with the current forever."

sentences.zh: 東南揚為大，刀布金玉積如阜，願公上天子常賦，頵請悉儲峙，單車以從。

translations.literal: The southeast takes Yangzhou as greatest; knives, cloth, gold, and jade pile like a mound; I beg you to send the emperor's regular tribute heavenward; Yun asks to store it all and follow with a single cart.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast holds Yangzhou greatest, with wealth heaped like a hill; send the emperor's tribute aloft—Yun will store it all and follow with one cart alone.

sentences.zh: 」行密答曰：「貢賦繇汴而達，適足資敵爾。

translations.literal: " Xingmi replied, "Tribute and taxes pass through Bian to arrive—enough only to enrich the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi answered, "Tribute goes through Bian and only feeds the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」於是頵絕行密，大募兵。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yun broke with Xingmi and raised troops on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Yun then broke with Xingmi and raised a great army.

sentences.zh: 李神福白行密：「頵必叛，宜先圖之。

translations.literal: Li Shenfu told Xingmi, "Yun is certain to rebel; we should plot against him first."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu warned Xingmi, "Yun will surely rebel; strike first."

sentences.zh: 」行密曰：「頵有大功，而反狀未明，殺之，諸將不為用。

translations.literal: " Xingmi said, "Yun has great merit, and his rebellion is not yet clear; to kill him, the generals will not serve."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi said, "Yun has great merit and his treason is not yet plain; kill him and the generals will not follow."

sentences.zh: 」頵遣其佐杜荀鶴至汴通好，全忠喜，屯宿州須變。

translations.literal: " Yun sent his aide Du Xunhe to Bian to propose friendship; Quanzhong was pleased and encamped at Suzhou awaiting the turn of events.
translations.idiomatic: Yun sent Du Xunhe to Bian for alliance; Quanzhong was pleased and camped at Suzhou awaiting events.

sentences.zh: 行密以康儒在頵所，故授廬州刺史以間之。

translations.literal: Xingmi, because Kang Ru was with Yun, therefore appointed him prefect of Luzhou to sow division.
translations.idiomatic: Because Kang Ru was with Yun, Xingmi made him prefect of Luzhou to divide them.

sentences.zh: 頵怒，族其家，儒曰：「公不用吾謀，死無地矣。」

translations.literal: Yun was enraged and executed his whole clan; Ru said, "If you will not use my plan, I shall have no place to die."
translations.idiomatic: Yun in fury slaughtered Ru's family; Ru said, "If you reject my counsel, I have nowhere to die."

sentences.zh: 頵與安仁義連和攻升州，劫刺史李神福妻息厚養之。

translations.literal: Yun joined An Renyi in attacking Shengzhou, seized the wife and children of prefect Li Shenfu, and kept them in generous care.
translations.idiomatic: Yun allied with An Renyi against Shengzhou, seized Li Shenfu's family, and treated them well.

sentences.zh: 神福方與劉存攻鄂州，行密召之。

translations.literal: Shenfu was then with Liu Cun attacking Ezhou; Xingmi summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu was attacking Ezhou with Liu Cun; Xingmi recalled him.

sentences.zh: 神福謂諸將曰：「頵反，此心腹疾，宜速攻之。

translations.literal: Shenfu told the generals, "Yun has rebelled; this is a disease of the vitals and should be attacked quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu told the generals, "Yun has rebelled—a mortal sickness of the heart; attack at once."

sentences.zh: 」頵遣李臯詒書神福曰：「公家在此，茍從我，當分地以王。

translations.literal: " Yun sent Li Gao with a deceitful letter to Shenfu saying, "Your family is here; if you will follow me, I shall divide territory and make you a king."
translations.idiomatic: Yun sent Li Gao with a forged letter: "Your family is here; join me and I will share the realm and make you a king."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「吾以一卒從吳王，任上將，終不以妻子易意。

translations.literal: " He answered, "I followed the Prince of Wu from a single soldier, was entrusted as a great general, and will never change my purpose for wife and children."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I followed the Prince of Wu from the ranks, was made a chief general, and will not shift loyalty for my family."

sentences.zh: 」乃斬臯，破頵兵於曷山。

translations.literal: " He then beheaded Gao and defeated Yun's troops at Yishan.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Gao and routed Yun's army at Yishan.

sentences.zh: 始，頵將王壇等以舟師躡神福後，至吉陽磯，不戰。

translations.literal: At first Yun's generals Wang Tan and others with the river force followed Shenfu's rear; reaching Jiyang Ford, they did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wang Tan and others with the fleet trailed Shenfu to Jiyang Ford and did not engage.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，壇掩神福軍半濟，神福反舟順流急擊，大破之，因縱火，士多死。

translations.literal: At dusk Tan struck Shenfu's army half across; Shenfu turned his boats downstream and struck swiftly, routing them greatly, then set fire, and many soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Tan hit the army mid-crossing; Shenfu reversed downstream and struck hard, broke them, set fire, and many perished.

sentences.zh: 明日，壇復戰，敗於皖口，頵乃自將來戰。

translations.literal: The next day Tan fought again and was defeated at Wankou; Yun then came in person to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Tan fought again and lost at Wankou; Yun then led the army himself.

sentences.zh: 神福曰：「賊棄城而來，此天亡也。

translations.literal: Shenfu said, "The rebels have abandoned their city to come—this is Heaven's destruction of them."
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu said, "The rebels left their walls to come—Heaven destroys them."

sentences.zh: 」乃瀕水堅壁不出，請行密以兵塞頵走道。

translations.literal: " He then walled along the water and would not come out, asking Xingmi to send troops to block Yun's escape route.
translations.idiomatic: He held the riverbank and would not emerge, asking Xingmi to block Yun's retreat.

sentences.zh: 仁義焚東塘戰艦，夜攻常州，不克，轉戰至夾岡，立二幟，解甲而息，追兵莫敢向。

translations.literal: Renyi burned the warships at Dongtang, attacked Changzhou by night without success, fought on to Jiagang, set up two banners, doffed armor to rest, and the pursuers dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi burned the Dongtang fleet, failed in a night assault on Changzhou, fought to Jiagang, raised two banners, doffed armor to rest, and pursuers dared not near.

sentences.zh: 頵陳舟蕪湖。

translations.literal: Yun arrayed boats at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Yun lined his boats at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 行密遣將王茂章攻潤州。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent the general Wang Maozhang to attack Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent Wang Maozhang against Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁義以善射冠軍中，當時稱朱瑾槊，米誌誠弩，皆為第一。

translations.literal: Renyi's skill at archery topped the army; at the time Zhu Jin's spear and Mi Zhicheng's crossbow were each called first.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi was the army's finest archer; Zhu Jin's spear and Mi Zhicheng's crossbow were then ranked first.

sentences.zh: 仁義常曰：「誌誠弩十，不當瑾槊之一；

translations.literal: Renyi often said, "Ten of Zhicheng's crossbows are not worth one of Jin's spears;"
translations.idiomatic: Renyi often said, "Ten of Zhicheng's bolts are not worth one thrust of Jin's spear;"

sentences.zh: 瑾槊十，不當吾弓之一。

translations.literal: ten of Jin's spears are not worth one of my bowshots.
translations.idiomatic: ten of Jin's spears are not worth one of my arrows."

sentences.zh: 」人以為然。

translations.literal: " People thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: People believed him.

sentences.zh: 又其治軍嚴，善得士心。

translations.literal: Moreover he governed the army strictly and knew how to win the soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He also ruled the army strictly and won the men's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 戰卒數百，濠梁不毀，開門鬥，先告所當中，然後射之。

translations.literal: With several hundred battle soldiers, the moat and bridge were not destroyed; opening the gate to fight, he first announced what he would hit, then shot.
translations.idiomatic: With hundreds of fighters he kept moat and bridge intact; opening the gate he named his target first, then shot.

sentences.zh: 茂章等不敢與確。

translations.literal: Maozhang and the others dared not engage him decisively.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhang and the rest dared not close with him.

sentences.zh: 行密遣使謂曰：「吾不忘公功，能自歸，當復為行軍副使，但不可處兵。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent a messenger saying, "I do not forget your merit; if you return of yourself, you shall again be acting army vice marshal, but you may not hold troops."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent word, "I remember your service; surrender and you shall be vice marshal again, but without troops."

sentences.zh: 」仁義欲降，其子固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: " Renyi wished to surrender; his son strongly remonstrated, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi wished to yield; his son dissuaded him and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 行密召其將臺濛泣語曰：「人嘗告頵必反，我不忍負人，頵果負我。

translations.literal: Xingmi summoned his general Tai Meng and said through tears, "People often told me Yun would surely rebel; I could not bear to wrong a man, and Yun has indeed wronged me.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi summoned Tai Meng in tears: "Men warned Yun would rebel; I would not wrong him, and he has wronged me.

sentences.zh: 吾思為將者非公莫可。

translations.literal: I think no one but you can be general.
translations.idiomatic: No one but you can command this army."

sentences.zh: 」濛頓首謝，率騎度江，為陣以行。

translations.literal: " Meng bowed his head in thanks, led his cavalry across the river, and advanced in formation.
translations.idiomatic: Meng bowed, led cavalry across the river, and marched in order.

sentences.zh: 士笑其怯，濛曰：「頵宿將多謀，備之何害？

translations.literal: The soldiers laughed at his timidity; Meng said, "Yun is an old commander full of stratagems—what harm in being prepared?"
translations.idiomatic: The men mocked his caution; Meng said, "Yun is a veteran of many plots—why not prepare?"

sentences.zh: 」與王壇等戰廣德，濛以行密書遺壇諸將，皆再拜氣奪。

translations.literal: " Fighting Wang Tan and others at Guangde, Meng sent Xingmi's letter to Tan's generals, and all bowed twice, their spirit broken.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangde he sent Xingmi's letter to Tan's officers; all bowed twice, their spirit broken.

sentences.zh: 濛麾兵擊之，壇走。

translations.literal: Meng waved the army forward and Tan fled.
translations.idiomatic: Meng charged and Tan fled.

sentences.zh: 神福既以不戰困頵，頵紿言母病，還至蕪湖。

translations.literal: Shenfu had already wearied Yun by not fighting; Yun falsely said his mother was ill and returned to Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu had worn Yun down by refusing battle; Yun feigned his mother's illness and returned to Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 聞壇敗，留精兵二萬屬郭行琮，身走城。

translations.literal: Hearing Tan was defeated, he left twenty thousand elite troops under Guo Xingqiong and himself hurried to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Tan's defeat, he left twenty thousand elites with Guo Xingqiong and raced to the city.

sentences.zh: 濛之行，為狹營小舍，覘者以為才容二千人，頵輕之，不復召兵。

translations.literal: On Meng's march he built narrow camps and small shelters; scouts thought they could hold only two thousand men; Yun despised them and did not summon more troops.
translations.idiomatic: Meng built small narrow camps; scouts thought only two thousand could fit; Yun scorned them and did not call up reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 與戰黃池，矢石始交而濛遁，兵爭逐北，遇伏，頵大敗，召蕪湖兵，不得入。

translations.literal: At Huangchi, as arrows and stones had just begun to fly Meng fled; the soldiers vied in pursuit northward, met an ambush, and Yun was greatly defeated; he called the Wuhu troops but could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangchi, as missiles flew Meng feigned flight; men chased north into ambush and Yun was routed; he called Wuhu's troops but they could not enter.

sentences.zh: 行琮及壇皆歸行密，頵恚，自料死士數百，號「爪牙都」，身薄戰。

translations.literal: Xingqiong and Tan both returned to Xingmi; Yun in rage selected several hundred death-fighters, called them the "Claw and Fang Company," and pressed the fight himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqiong and Tan submitted to Xingmi; Yun in wrath picked hundreds of death-fighters as the "Claw and Fang Company" and fought in person.

sentences.zh: 濛退軍示弱，士超隍，濛殊死戰，軍潰。

translations.literal: Meng withdrew showing weakness; the men leaped the moat; Meng fought desperately and the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Meng feigned weakness; men stormed the moat; Meng fought desperately and the army broke.

sentences.zh: 頵奔城，橋陷，為亂兵所殺，年四十六。

translations.literal: Yun fled toward the city; the bridge gave way and he was killed by the disorderly troops at forty-six years of age.
translations.idiomatic: Yun ran for the city; the bridge collapsed and disorderly soldiers killed him at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 其下猶鬥，示頵首，乃潰。

translations.literal: His men still fought; when Yun's head was shown, they then scattered.
translations.idiomatic: His men still fought until Yun's head was displayed; then they fled.

sentences.zh: 頵始以元瓘歸，戰不勝，輒欲殺之，頵母護免。

translations.literal: At first when Yuan Guan was sent back, whenever the battle went badly Yun wished to kill him, but Yun's mother protected him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Guan was first sent as hostage, Yun after each defeat wished to kill him; Yun's mother shielded him.

sentences.zh: 及镠與行密合，頵曰：「今日不勝，必殺元瓘。

translations.literal: When Liu and Xingmi joined forces, Yun said, "If we do not win today, I shall surely kill Yuan Guan."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu and Xingmi united, Yun said, "If we lose today, Yuan Guan dies."

sentences.zh: 」已而頵死，傳首至淮南，行密泣下，葬以庶人禮，亦葬康儒，還元瓘於杭。

translations.literal: " Soon Yun died; his head was sent to Huainan; Xingmi wept, buried him with commoner rites, also buried Kang Ru, and returned Yuan Guan to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yun soon died; his head reached Huainan; Xingmi wept, buried him as a commoner, buried Kang Ru, and sent Yuan Guan back to Hang.

sentences.zh: 頵善為治，資寬厚，通利商賈，民愛之。

translations.literal: Yun was skilled in governance, by nature generous and tolerant, promoted merchants, and the people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun governed well, was generous by nature, favored trade, and the people loved him.

sentences.zh: 善遇士，若楊夔、康軿、夏侯淑、殷文圭、王希羽等皆為上客。

translations.literal: He treated scholars well; Yang Kui, Kang Ping, Xiahou Shu, Yin Wengui, Wang Xiyu, and others were all honored guests.
translations.idiomatic: He treated men of letters generously; Yang Kui, Kang Ping, Xiahou Shu, Yin Wengui, Wang Xiyu, and others were all his chief guests.

sentences.zh: 文圭有美名，全忠、镠交辟不應。

translations.literal: Wengui had a fine reputation; Quanzhong and Liu both repeatedly summoned him, but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wengui enjoyed a fine reputation; Quanzhong and Liu both courted him repeatedly, but he would not answer.

sentences.zh: 頵置田宅，迎其母，以甥事之，故文圭為盡力。

translations.literal: Yun set up fields and houses, welcomed his mother, and treated her as a maternal aunt; therefore Wengui gave his full effort.
translations.idiomatic: Yun granted him lands and a house, welcomed his mother, and treated her as his own aunt by marriage; Wengui therefore served him with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 夔知頵不足亢行密，著《溺賦》以戒，頵不用。

translations.literal: Kui knew Yun could not match Xingmi, composed the "Fu on Drowning" as a warning, but Yun did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: Kui saw that Yun could not stand against Xingmi and wrote the "Fu on Drowning" as a warning, but Yun ignored it.

sentences.zh: 行密使王茂章穴地取潤州，安仁義以家屬保城樓，兵不敢登。

translations.literal: Xingmi had Wang Maozhang tunnel underground to take Runzhou; An Renyi sheltered his family on the city tower, and the soldiers dared not climb.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi had Wang Maozhang tunnel into Runzhou; An Renyi sheltered his family on the tower, and the troops dared not ascend.

sentences.zh: 召李德誠曰：「汝可以委命。

translations.literal: He summoned Li Decheng and said, "You may entrust your life."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Li Decheng and said, "You may surrender your life to me."

sentences.zh: 」乃抵弓矢就縛，父子斬揚州市。

translations.literal: " He then handed over bow and arrows and submitted to binding; father and son were beheaded in the Yangzhou market.
translations.idiomatic: He handed over his bow and arrows to be bound; father and son were beheaded in the Yangzhou marketplace.

sentences.zh: 濛，字頂雲，亦合肥人。

translations.literal: Meng, styled Dingyun, was also a native of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, courtesy name Dingyun, was also from Hefei.

sentences.zh: 頵破，行密表為檢校太保、宣州觀察使。

translations.literal: When Yun was broken, Xingmi memorialized him as acting Grand Guardian and military commissioner of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Yun's defeat, Xingmi recommended him as acting Grand Guardian and commissioner of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 天祐初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Tianyou era.

sentences.zh: 朱延壽者，廬州舒城人。

translations.literal: Zhu Yanshou was a native of Shucheng in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yanshou was from Shucheng in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 事行密，破秦彥、畢師鐸、趙锽、孫儒功居多。

translations.literal: Serving Xingmi, in defeating Qin Yan, Bi Shiduo, Zhao Chuan, and Sun Ru his merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingmi's service, his merit was greatest in defeating Qin Yan, Bi Shiduo, Zhao Chuan, and Sun Ru.

sentences.zh: 行密欲以寬恕結人心，而延壽敢殺。

translations.literal: Xingmi wished to win hearts through leniency, but Yanshou dared to kill.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi wished to bind hearts through mercy, yet Yanshou dared to execute men.

sentences.zh: 時揚州多盜，捕得者，行密輒賜所盜遣之，戒曰：「勿使延壽知。

translations.literal: At that time Yangzhou had many thieves; when they were captured, Xingmi would bestow what they had stolen and release them, warning, "Do not let Yanshou know."
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou then had many thieves; when caught, Xingmi would return their loot and release them, warning, "Do not let Yanshou know."

sentences.zh: 」已而陰許延壽殺之。

translations.literal: " Yet secretly he permitted Yanshou to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in secret he allowed Yanshou to kill them.

sentences.zh: 初，壽州刺史高彥溫舉州入朱全忠，行密襲之，諸將憚城堅不可拔，延壽鼓之，拔其城即表為淮南節度副使。

translations.literal: Initially Shouzhou prefect Gao Yanwen surrendered the whole prefecture to Zhu Quanzhong; Xingmi attacked it; the generals feared the strong walls could not be taken; Yanshou roused them, took the city, and was immediately memorialized as vice military governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shouzhou prefect Gao Yanwen surrendered the prefecture to Quanzhong; Xingmi attacked; the generals feared the stout walls; Yanshou urged them on, took the city, and was at once made vice governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 全忠猶屯壽春，延壽以新軍出，每旗五伍為列，遣李厚以十旗擊西偏，不勝，將斬之，厚請益五旗，殊死戰，全忠引去。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was still encamped at Shouchun; Yanshou led fresh troops out; each banner formed ranks of five; he sent Li Hou with ten banners to strike the western flank; not victorious, he was about to behead him; Hou asked for five more banners, fought desperately, and Quanzhong withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong still held Shouchun; Yanshou led fresh troops out in ranks of five per banner; Li Hou with ten banners struck the west wing and failed; Yanshou was about to execute him; Hou begged five more banners, fought to the death, and Quanzhong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是取黃、蘄、光三州，以功遷壽州團練使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took the three prefectures of Huang, Qi, and Guang; for his merit he was transferred to military training commissioner of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Huang, Qi, and Guang; for this he was made military training commissioner of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 昭宗在鳳翔，詔延壽圍蔡以披全忠勢，擢奉國軍節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong was at Fengxiang; an edict ordered Yanshou to besiege Cai to relieve Quanzhong's pressure, and he was promoted to military governor of the Fengguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Zhaozong was at Fengxiang, an edict ordered Yanshou to besiege Cai and ease Quanzhong's plight; he was promoted governor of the Fengguo Army.

sentences.zh: 全忠兵每至，延壽開門不設備，而不敢逼也。

translations.literal: Whenever Quanzhong's troops arrived, Yanshou opened the gates without preparing defenses, yet they dared not press him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Quanzhong's army came, Yanshou opened the gates without defense, yet they dared not press him.

sentences.zh: 延壽用軍常以寡鬥眾，敗還者盡斬之。

translations.literal: Yanshou in using troops often fought many with few; those who returned defeated were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou often fought many with few; any who returned defeated were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 田頵之附全忠，延壽陰約曰：「公有所為，我願執鞭。

translations.literal: When Tian Yun attached himself to Quanzhong, Yanshou secretly pledged, "Whatever you undertake, I wish to serve at your whip."
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Yun joined Quanzhong, Yanshou secretly pledged, "Whatever you do, I will serve at your whip."

sentences.zh: 」頵喜，二人謀絕行密。

translations.literal: " Yun was pleased; the two plotted to break with Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was pleased, and the two plotted to cut off Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 行密憂甚，紿病目，行觸柱僵。

translations.literal: Xingmi was deeply worried; he feigned illness of the eyes, walked, struck a pillar, and fell stiff.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi was deeply troubled; he feigned blindness, walked into a pillar, and fell as if dead.

sentences.zh: 妻，延壽姊也，掖之。

translations.literal: His wife was Yanshou's elder sister and supported him.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Yanshou's elder sister, helped him up.

sentences.zh: 行密泣曰：「吾喪明，諸子幼，得舅代我，無憂矣。

translations.literal: Xingmi wept and said, "I have lost my sight; my sons are young; if I obtain my uncle-in-law to replace me, I need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi wept, "I am blind; my sons are young; with my uncle-in-law to replace me, I need not worry."

sentences.zh: 」遣辯士召之，延壽疑，不肯赴。

translations.literal: " He sent a persuader to summon him; Yanshou doubted and would not come.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an envoy to summon him; Yanshou suspected a trap and would not come.

sentences.zh: 姊遣婢報故，延壽疾走揚州，拜未訖，士禽殺之，而廢其妻。

translations.literal: His sister sent a maid to report the truth; Yanshou rushed to Yangzhou; before the bow was finished soldiers seized and killed him, and his wife was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: His sister sent a maid with the truth; Yanshou raced to Yangzhou; before his bow was complete soldiers seized and killed him, and his wife was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：全忠，唐之盜也，行密誌梟其元而後已。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Quanzhong was a thief of Tang; Xingmi resolved to behead him and would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Quanzhong was Tang's robber; Xingmi vowed to take his head and would not rest.

sentences.zh: 田頵使出軍賦而助之，此其謀責難而絕之，非忠於唐也。

translations.literal: Tian Yun sent out military levies to aid him; in this his stratagem was to press for blame and break away—this was not loyalty to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yun sent levies to aid him; his aim was to press for tribute and break away—not loyalty to Tang.

sentences.zh: 棄所附而覬尊大，亦已妄矣。

translations.literal: To abandon whom one followed and covet higher honor was already deluded.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon one's patron and covet greater standing was folly enough.

sentences.zh: 孔子稱孟公綽為趙、魏老則優，不可以為滕、薛大夫。

translations.literal: Confucius said that Meng Gongchuo would excel as steward of Zhao and Wei but could not serve as steward of Teng and Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said Meng Gongchuo would excel as steward for Zhao and Wei but could not serve Teng and Xue.

sentences.zh: 如仁厚、田、朱，材不足為吳、蜀之老，可與事天子哉！

translations.literal: Men like Renhou, Tian, and Zhu lacked the talent to be stewards of Wu and Shu—how could they serve the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Men like Renhou, Tian, and Zhu were not fit to be stewards for Wu and Shu—how could they serve the emperor!
